request.spec:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Review assignment is in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` now pass. The main "review assignment" test passed on the first run. Scenarios 1 and 3 kept failing on three bugs that were already in the app, so I fixed those too.

**The feature**
- **Stored data:** migration `V108__claim_review_assigned.sql` adds a `review_assigned` column to claims. The claim keeps the assigned user after it leaves REVIEW, which the test expects. Clone and transfer copy the column along with the claim.
- **Server:** a new endpoint `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/review-assign`, defined in YAML with one small class per step, following the existing remind endpoint.
  - It refuses a blank user, a claim that isn't REVIEW, and anyone who isn't a steward. A user acting as steward by delegation is allowed.
  - A refusal writes nothing.
  - On success it writes `REVIEW_ASSIGNED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=… user=<user>`. When the user is acting by delegation, the existing audit service adds `for=<steward>` at the end.
- **Front end:**
  - Each claim row shows the assigned user (`claim-review-assigned`) and has an entry and button (`claim-review-user`, `claim-review-assign`).
  - A refusal shows the existing `claim-error`, which clears when the entry is changed or the action is retried.
  - The header shows `my-reviews-count`: the REVIEW claims assigned to the signed-in user.

**Bugs I fixed along the way**
1. **Bulk settle gave the wrong claim numbers.** It dry-runs every claim to check whether any would be refused, and that dry run used up numbers, so two claims got FY2026-3 and -4 instead of -1 and -2. The check now gives no numbers (`SettleClaims.java`).
2. **As-of views dropped opening balances.** The table of openings was the only history table missing from the list the as-of view rebuilds, so carried figures showed 0.00 instead of 1.00 (`AsOf.java`).
3. **The last batch number disappeared after a transfer.** It was worked out only from the sheet's claims, and transferring a person deletes their claims from the sheet. A later bulk settle would also have reused batch 1. The sheet now keeps its last batch in a new table (`V109__sheet_batch.sql`), and that value is included when the sheet is loaded and in as-of views.

Fixes 2 and 3 touch features outside this change request, so you may want to look at them separately.
